findings.classification: Established false unrestricted auxiliary proposition; actual restricted newvector use admits a local repair

anchors.location: use for d_n,j in the local-class construction

findings.exact_claim: Under absence of a pole of L(pi,s) at s=1, an arbitrary Kirillov function phi is asserted to have a unique smooth xi whose restriction near zero lies in the Kirillov model and for which (1-diag(p,1))xi=phi.

counterexample.parameters: Take p=3 and a nontrivial ramified quadratic character eta of Q_3^x, with eta(3)=1. Put chi_1=|.|_3^(-1)eta and take chi_2 unramified with chi_2(3)=2. Let pi=Ind_lower(chi_1 tensor chi_2), in the paper's unnormalized convention.
counterexample.irreducibility: chi_1/chi_2 is ramified, hence is not one of the exceptional unramified ratios for reducible principal series. The representation is irreducible and infinite-dimensional as required.
counterexample.no_pole: The ramified chi_1 contributes no local Euler factor. In the paper's convention the other factor is (1-p*chi_2(p)*p^(-s))^(-1)=(1-2*p^(1-s))^(-1). At s=1 its denominator is -1, so the stated no-pole hypothesis holds.
counterexample.kirillov_membership: Page 19 gives phi_f(x)=|x|chi_1(x) Fourier(f)(x)=eta(x) Fourier(f)(x). For every integer m, take f_m=p^(-m)1_(p^(-m)Z_p). With volume(Z_p)=1, Fourier(f_m)=1_(p^m Z_p), so eta(x)1_(p^m Z_p)(x) belongs to the Kirillov model. Compactly supported locally constant functions on Q_p^x also belong by the same Fourier realization.
counterexample.equation: P acts as xi(x)->xi(px). Since eta(px)=eta(x), xi_i(x)-xi_i(px)=eta(x)[1_{v(x)<=0}-1_{v(x)+1<=0}]=eta(x)1_{v(x)=0}=phi(x), for i=0 and i=1.
counterexample.local_restrictions: For a ball p^m Z_p, the truncated xi_0 is zero if m>0, and otherwise equals eta(1_(p^m Z_p)-1_(p Z_p)). The corresponding truncated xi_1 adds eta1_(p^m Z_p). All are in the Kirillov model. A general compact open neighborhood differs from such a ball by a compact subset of Q_p^x, which again gives a Kirillov function.
counterexample.distinctness: xi_1-xi_0=eta is nonzero. Thus the asserted uniqueness fails even with all stated no-pole and local-germ conditions.
counterexample.extra_clauses: phi is not invariant under the regular unit action, so the proposition's conditional Gamma-invariance clause does not exclude either solution. The angular average of eta is zero; both solutions also give the same zero Mellin/outer-unit average in the final identity.
counterexample.proof_error: The proof's reduction to unramified geometric tails omits ramified unit types. Also, a homogeneous p-shift-invariant difference need not have support bounded away from infinity: the proposition requires only local Kirillov membership near zero, not global Kirillov support.

actual_use_and_repair: The actual d_n,j has an unramified radial germ, with regular unit weight -j, once x is sufficiently small. Restrict the chosen inverse to this finite-dimensional germ space.

The shift eigenvalues on that germ space are alpha_i/p^(j+1); no pole at j+1 excludes 1. Inverting 1-P on this space, including repeated-root Jordan blocks, and extending by annular recursion gives the needed selected inverse germ.

This corrects the quantifier and uniqueness normalization needed for the newvector use. It does not prove the original proposition for arbitrary Kirillov functions, and the generalized p-adic comparison/lifting is still the cited external input.
No counterexample to the main constant-scaled theorem or to the actual c_n,j is claimed from this local counterexample.
findings.severity_scope: The parent should calibrate the false lemma and its use in the core local construction under the review contract. Repairability does not make the original universal statement true.

findings.classification: Established prime-2 counterexamples to Lemmas 9.2.2 and 9.2.3 in the actual coefficient algebra

anchors.location: Section 8.1 definition of L, O_L and Lambda
reflexive hull and full Lambda construction

coefficient_scope: Section 8.1 defines L/Q_p as the field generated by the Fourier coefficients and Lambda=O_L[[Gal(Q(mu_(p^infinity))/Q)]], not merely the algebra of an open procyclic subgroup.

No decomposition into an integral character component or odd-prime hypothesis precedes Lemma 9.2.2 or Lemma 9.2.3. The full text was read, the relevant original pages were inspected, and a complete text index search found no odd-prime restriction.

The examples below work for every finite extension O of Z_2, with uniformizer varpi and finite residue field k. Thus they are not dependent on choosing a coefficient ring outside the stated O_L class.
findings.ring: At p=2, Gal(Q(mu_(2^infinity))/Q)=C_2 x (1+4Z_2). Hence R=Lambda=O[[X,U]]/(U^2+2U), where 1+U represents the element s of C_2. R is free of rank two over O[[X]], so varpi is a non-zero-divisor. Its maximal ideal is m=(varpi,U,X).

lemma_9_2_2_counterexample.hypotheses: Y is finitely generated, is killed by the non-zero-divisor varpi, and hence is R-torsion in the usual sense. Every nonzero R-submodule is a nonzero k[[X]]-ideal, necessarily X^a k[[X]], which is infinite. Therefore Y has no nonzero finite R-submodule.
lemma_9_2_2_counterexample.fitting: Its zeroth Fitting ideal is I=(varpi,U), from the one-row presentation of this cyclic quotient.
lemma_9_2_2_counterexample.nonprincipality: Let n=(varpi,U,X) in the regular power-series ring O[[X,U]]. The defining relation U^2+2U lies in n^2 because 2 is divisible by varpi. Therefore m/m^2 has independent k-basis classes varpi,U,X. Since mI is contained in m^2, the classes of varpi and U in I/mI are independent; they also generate it. Thus dim_k(I/mI)=2. Nakayama's lemma implies I requires two generators and is not principal, contrary to the explicit conclusion of Lemma 9.2.2.

lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.ideals: Take A=m and I=varpi R. Then I is contained in A and R/A=k is finite, exactly the finite-index hypothesis in Lemma 9.2.3.
lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.module: M=A/I is the ideal (U,X) in S=R/varpi R=k[[X,U]]/(U^2). It has generators e1=[U], e2=[X].
lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.complete_relations: A full relation matrix has columns (varpi,0), (0,varpi), (U+2,0), (-X,U). To check completeness modulo varpi, write a=a0(X)+Ua1(X), b=b0(X)+Ub1(X). The relation aU+bX=0 gives b0 X=0 and a0+b1 X=0, hence b0=0 and a0=-b1 X. Thus the syzygies over S are generated by (U,0) and (-X,U); lifting adds precisely the two varpi-relations.
lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.minors: The 2-by-2 minors are varpi^2, 0, varpi U, -varpi(U+2), varpi X, and U(U+2)=0. Since 2 lies in varpi O, they generate varpi(varpi,U,X)=varpi m. Hence Fitt_R(A/I)=varpi m.
lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.failure: varpi is not in varpi m, because varpi is a non-zero-divisor and 1 is not in m. Therefore I is not contained in Fitt_R(A/I), directly contradicting the conclusion of Lemma 9.2.3.
lemma_9_2_3_counterexample.no_finite_submodule: Although Lemma 9.2.3 does not separately assume it, this example also has no nonzero finite submodule: M=k[[X]]U direct-sum Xk[[X]] as a k[[X]]-module, so X acts injectively and a nonzero submodule is infinite.

impact_and_repair: This is a failure of the exact universal algebraic results used in Lemma 9.2.4 and the Fitting proof, not merely a missing explanation of a characteristic-ideal convention.

For odd p, the finite torsion subgroup has order p-1 invertible in O, so the standard character-component regular-ring argument applies. An explicit odd-prime restriction removes this particular counterexample.

Retaining p=2 requires a replacement proof over an open procyclic algebra and an integral comparison with the full group ring, or suitable additional projective-dimension/control hypotheses. A uniform scalar in the main theorem might allow such a repair, but no complete prime-2 repair is established here.
The counterexamples are to the algebraic lemmas; they are not presented as explicit modular-form counterexamples to Theorem A.
findings.provenance: The second, direct Lemma 9.2.3 example was proposed by parent /root and independently checked here by the complete syzygy and minor computation. The first example and the original full-ring boundary check were derived by this helper.

findings.classification: Established internal mismatch between the printed sign-projector definition and the claimed interpolation normalization

anchors.location: Section 10.1 definitions of lambda-plus/minus and phi

findings.printed_definitions: The source sets lambda_plus(a)=lambda(a)+lambda(-a), lambda_minus(a)=lambda(a)-lambda(-a), and phi(a)=lambda_plus(a)/Omega_plus+lambda_minus(a)/Omega_minus. There is no factor 1/2 and no (-1)^j in the printed sign projections.
derivation: For a primitive character chi of G_n, let epsilon=chi(-1) in {+1,-1}, and S_chi=sum_a chi(a)^(-1)lambda(a). Replacing a by -a gives sum_a chi(a)^(-1)lambda(-a)=epsilon S_chi.
The literal definitions therefore give chi(theta_an)=[(1+epsilon)/Omega_plus+(1-epsilon)/Omega_minus]S_chi=2 S_chi/Omega_epsilon.
The usual Mellin/Fourier identity for the displayed integral gives S_chi=chi(-1) j! p^(nj) tau(chi^(-1)) L(f,chi,j+1)/(-2pi i)^j.

Formula (18), however, is S_chi/Omega_{(-1)^j epsilon}. For every even j the printed definitions differ by an exact factor 2; for odd j the period label is also exchanged. This is a formal algebraic inconsistency, not a numerical guess about an L-value.
findings.correction: To obtain the displayed interpolation convention while keeping the formula phi=lambda_plus/Omega_plus+lambda_minus/Omega_minus, replace the projections by lambda_plus/minus(a)=[lambda(a) +/- (-1)^j lambda(-a)]/2, and normalize the cohomological periods consistently with those projections.
scope: This correction is local to the analytic definitions and their period convention. It must be carried through the later comparison constants; the original literal definitions are not silently changed in this review.
A factor 2 can be absorbed by a fixed scalar in a weak theorem, but the parity-dependent period label should be stated correctly, rather than described as only a factor-2 issue.
No modular L-value was numerically assumed nonzero to identify the formula mismatch. The exact finite-character algebra is independently corroborated in independent_checks.json.
The finding does not by itself establish that the intended constant-scaled main theorem is false.

per_problem.source: PDF pp.19,21-22; p.25; actual newvector use pp.28-30
per_problem.verdict: Confirmed false unrestricted uniqueness statement; its restricted intended use admits the stated local repair.
per_problem.hypothesis_and_witness_check: At p=3 choose a nontrivial ramified quadratic eta with eta(3)=1, chi1=|.|^-1 eta and unramified chi2(3)=2. The ratio is ramified and excludes the exceptional reducibility ratios. In the source's lower-Borel convention the only Euler factor is (1-2 p^(1-s))^-1 and has no pole at 1. The p.19 Fourier model gives eta times Fourier(f); f_m=p^-m 1_(p^-m Zp) produces eta 1_(p^m Zp). Thus the two locally Kirillov functions xi0=eta 1_(v(x)<=0) and xi1=xi0+eta have the same (1-P) image eta 1_(v=0) and are distinct. Every compact-open near-zero truncation lies in the model; no global support condition is in Proposition 6.4.1. The conditional regular-unit invariance clause does not apply, and eta has zero angular average.
per_problem.repair_and_counterevidence: For the actual translated newvector the near-zero germ has regular weight -j and unramified radial tails. Eigenvalues alpha_i/p^(j+1) exclude one by the no-pole hypothesis; (I-rI-N)^-1=sum N^h/(1-r)^(h+1) handles repeated roots. Extend the selected inverse germ annulus by annulus, retaining the j! visible in (9). This establishes the needed normalization of the germ, not the false arbitrary-function proposition. The generalized lifting remains an external input. No counterexample to the constructed arithmetic classes is asserted.

per_problem.source: PDF p.37 full Lambda definition; pp.40-42 Lemmas 9.2.2-9.2.4 and Theorem 9.1.1
per_problem.verdict: Confirmed exact universal algebraic failures at the permitted prime two.
per_problem.hypothesis_and_witness_check: For every coefficient DVR O over Z2, R=O[[X,U]]/(U(U+2)) is free rank two over O[[X]], so varpi is regular. Y=R/(varpi,U)=k[[X]] is finitely generated torsion and has no nonzero finite submodule. Its Fitting ideal (varpi,U) needs two generators by m/m^2 and Nakayama. For A=m=(varpi,U,X), I=varpi R, R/A is finite. Reducing aU+bX=0 modulo varpi in k[[X]][U]/U^2 gives precisely syzygies (U,0),(-X,U); lifting adds the two varpi relations. The complete 2x4 matrix has minors generating varpi m. Since varpi is regular, varpi does not lie in varpi m. Thus I is not contained in Fitt(A/I), even though this M also has no finite submodule.
per_problem.impact_and_repair: Source p.42 actually uses both the characteristic/Fitting equality and Lemma 9.2.4. These are auxiliary algebra counterexamples, not modular-form counterexamples to Theorem A. For odd p the torsion factor is integrally split into regular two-dimensional power-series components, which removes these examples. Retaining p=2 needs an integral comparison/replacement argument; no complete prime-two repair is claimed. The native bounded check read the full coefficient scope and found no odd-prime restriction; the primary checked the actual Lambda definition and lemma hypotheses.

per_problem.source: PDF pp.42-43, definitions and (18); pp.45-46 comparison
per_problem.verdict: Confirmed normalization mismatch with a precise local correction.
per_problem.reasoning: Let epsilon=chi(-1) and S=sum chi(a)^-1 lambda(a). Reindexing a to -a gives the second sum epsilon S. The literal unhalved projectors therefore yield 2S/Omega_epsilon. The claimed interpolation instead gives S/Omega_((-1)^j epsilon). The highest critical point for even k>=4 has even j=k-2 and s=k-1>(k+1)/2, so the cited Ramanujan bound gives an absolutely convergent nonzero twisted Euler product, providing genuine nonzero instances of the factor-two discrepancy. The source's sign formula is not silently replaced.
per_problem.repair_and_impact: The projectors [lambda(a) +/- (-1)^j lambda(-a)]/2 yield exactly the stated sign and factor. The change must be propagated through cohomological/Kato periods and comparison constants. A fixed factor two can be absorbed in the weak main theorem's scalar; that does not validate the parity label or the printed central identification. No intended main-theorem counterexample is asserted.
